title: Microbudget flows — mini PRD / jot
content:
Top-level idea: give app developers fine-grained, per-interaction token budgets and graceful degradation policies so apps can guarantee predictable spend and SLAs under brittle or bursty workloads.

Why:
- Customers keep asking for predictable unit-cost controls that don't require full model changes or dedicated capacity.
- Rapidly helps product teams cap spend for experiments, free tiers, and microtransactions.
- Complements batching/caching suggestions in Optimize — policy layer on top of runtime.

Key goals (MVP):
1) Allow a request-level budget expressed in tokens (prompt + completion) or cost units.
2) If budget would be exceeded mid-generation, runtime must: optional truncation / switch to cheaper model / return partial response + signal.
3) Expose SDK + REST flags and Console UI to set per-route defaults and fallbacks.
4) Telemetry: per-request cost estimate, budget-strike events, and user-visible labels for why a response was truncated/ downgraded.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Automatic model rewrites or prompt condensation (nice-to-have later).
- Billing-level metering changes (we surface events; billing remains per-token for now).

User personas / stories:
- Growth engineer (free tier experiment): "I want each free-user chat to consume <= 150 tokens on average; if not, degrade to concise mode so spend is bounded."
- Product manager (A/B): "Run a test with budget 300 vs 600 tokens per convo to measure engagement delta and cost uplift."
- Platform admin (enterprise): "Enforce hard caps per-API-key to avoid runaway third-party integrations."

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API accepts budget param: "budget_tokens" (int) and "budget_behavior" (soft|strict|fallback-model).
- When soft and budget approached: runtime returns a header X-Estimated-Cost and a final response flag "budget_exhausted":true with partial text.
- When strict: model generation stops before exceeding budget; response has 402-like structured reason in error field.
- When fallback-model: automatically route to pre-configured cheaper variant (e.g., quantized / smaller model) and include metadata about switch.
- Console shows per-route default budget, history of budget events, and quick-create policy templates.

Implementation sketch (runtime + control plane):
- Request path: pre-calc prompt token estimate (use tokenizer heuristics) + requested completion budget. If predicted total > budget, act per behavior.
- Streaming: emit budget remaining updates in stream meta events so clients can stop early if desired.
- Fallback model routing: route policy table keyed by customer-plan + route + active budget profile. Must be near-zero added latency.
- Metrics: budget_hit_count, budget_hit_rate_per_route, avg_tokens_saved, fallback_switch_rate.

SDK surface ideas (quick):
- JS/py: client.generate({model, prompt, budget_tokens:150, budget_behavior:'fallback-model', fallback_model:'redwood-medium-q4'}).
- Console: route-level toggle + per-key override.

UX / client implications:
- Clients should handle partial responses and present a UI affordance like "Continue (may cost extra)".
- Provide a helper to auto-retry with higher budget if user confirms.
- For chat: budget should be applied per-turn or per-session? Default: per-turn to keep semantics simple; add session-budget later.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost predictability: tokenizer heuristics can mis-estimate; false negatives cause surprise. Need conservative margin and post-hoc reconciliation.
- Bad developer experience if too many silent downgrades. Must surface a clear audit trail and console logs.
- Billing mismatch: if fallback model costs more in tokens but cheaper per-token price (rare), need to reconcile displayed cost vs billed cost.
- Interaction with prefix KV caching / batching: budget enforcement must consider cached prompt token reduction.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (internal): SDK flag + runtime stub for soft/strict; collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
- Beta (selected customers): add fallback-model routing + console UI templates; collect UX feedback.
- GA: add templates, guardrails for enterprise tenants, and billing reconciliation docs.

Experiment matrix / metrics to watch:
- Primary: budget_hit_rate, average_tokens_per_request, change in user engagement for A/B.
notes_to_self: TODO: sketch console wireframes, confirm tokenizer lib for all public models, sync with billing on event schema, write up quick-runbook for SRE for fallback storms. Consider pairing with 'prefix-coverage' feature from Optimize to get better estimates.
